subject: Clarification on Commit Tiers, Overages & PO Vendor Form
messages:
From: Karen Lin <karen.lin@brightgrid.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Vendor form + pricing clarification for Hosted API commit

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked solid. Procurement has one blocking question before we can route a PO: we need to understand how Redwood handles commit tiers vs. overage billing and whether you can sign our preferred vendor form (attached). Specific items they called out:

- Do committed tokens carry a per-token discounted rate, and how are tier breakpoints defined?
- If BrightGrid goes over the monthly commit, what rate applies to overages and how are they invoiced?
- BrightGrid policy requires a signed vendor form as the legal instrument for POs; is that acceptable or do you need Redwood T&Cs signed separately?
- What is your invoicing cadence and standard payment terms (BrightGrid prefers Net-60 if possible)?

Attached is our vendor form (BrightGrid_VendorForm_Filled.pdf). Procurement also asked for a W-9 and SOC2 report — can you share those?

Thanks,
Karen Lin
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightGrid, Inc.
[attachment: BrightGrid_VendorForm_Filled.pdf]
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Karen Lin <karen.lin@brightgrid.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor form + pricing clarification for Hosted API commit

Hi Karen — appreciate the clear list. We're happy to work through this. Quick answers up front, and I'll follow with a fuller proposal and a short call if that helps:

- Commit tiers: yes — committed monthly token volumes map to a per-token discounted rate. We typically propose 3 tiers (1M, 5M, 20M tokens/month) with step discounts. See the attached pricing matrix and a draft commit schedule.
- Overages: overages are billed monthly at the standard pay-as-you-go rate unless otherwise negotiated; we can agree a cap or blended overage rate for enterprise commits.
- Vendor form: we can accept your vendor form for PO setup (vendor name, remit details), but we require our MSA (or an explicitly referenced set of terms) to govern service terms. I can outline the minimal legal fields we need to keep in our MSA to be comfortable accepting your PO form.
- Invoicing: monthly invoicing, standard is net-45; net-60 is possible for enterprise clients on a credit-approved basis — we can escalate.

I've attached: redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx and Redwood_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf for examples. Would you have 30 minutes next week to walk procurement through the billing language?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
[attachments: redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx, Redwood_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf]
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Vendor form + pricing clarification — suggested negotiation posture

Vanessa / Priyom — forwarding Karen's vendor form and Vanessa's note. Procurement is insisting on vendor-form-first approach; that tends to be the sticking point. My suggested posture:

1) Commercial concessions we can offer without legal approval:
   - 12-month committed term with a 12% blended token discount vs. list for the committed volume (tiered breakpoints as Vanessa noted).
   - Overages billed at pay-as-you-go rate but eligible for a 5% discount if cumulative monthly overage <30% of the commit; otherwise standard GPO rate.

2) Legal posture: accept the vendor form for PO/vendor onboarding only, but require execution of our MSA or a short SOW referencing our T&Cs to avoid exposing product/service-level liabilities.

3) Finance/ops asks: provide daily token usage exports and a monthly invoice with token-level line items. Procurement asked for SOC2 — we can share our SOC2 Type II report under an NDA; we should check if BrightGrid requires an attestation copy.

If legal wants to relax net-45 to net-60, I'd like an offset (e.g., 2% discount reduction) unless we get a prepayment or deposit. Priyom, please confirm if vendor form acceptance subject to our MSA is acceptable.

-Rafael
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Karen Lin <karen.lin@brightgrid.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor form + pricing clarification for Hosted API commit

Karen — thanks for sending the form. After a quick internal review, here's a concrete proposal to unblock procurement while protecting both parties:

Proposal overview:
- Commit tiers (example): 1M/month => $0.0009 per token (10% discount); 5M/month => $0.00076 per token (15% discount); 20M/month => $0.00064 per token (20% discount). Detailed tier sheet attached.
- Overages: billed monthly. Standard pay-as-you-go rate is $0.0010 per token. For customers on a 12-month committed plan we can offer a blended overage rate equal to the committed tier rate + 5% (i.e., lower than list but above committed).
- Vendor form: Redwood can accept BrightGrid's vendor form to create the vendor record and issue POs. However, the PO will explicitly reference Redwood's MSA (or the enclosed SOW) for service terms and liabilities. We will not accept the vendor form as a substitute for the MSA. If procurement requires the vendor form to be the primary legal agreement, we will need a short review and limited redline.
- Invoicing & payment terms: monthly invoices with token-line detail. Standard net-45; we can review net-60 for enterprise finance after credit/FS checks.

Attachments and next steps:
- Attached: Redwood_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf (example SOW-level schedule) and redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx.
- I've also uploaded a draft DocuSign link for execution if you want to accept this approach: https://docusign.net/sign/BG-2026-137

If BrightGrid is comfortable accepting the vendor form for PO + signing our MSA (or a short-form SOW pointing to our terms), we can run procurement and finance in parallel and aim to have a PO by mid-December. Happy to hop on a call to walk procurement through the invoice/export format.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachments: Redwood_Commit_Schedule_v2.pdf, redwood_pricing_matrix.xlsx]
From: Karen Lin <karen.lin@brightgrid.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor form + pricing clarification for Hosted API commit

Vanessa — thanks for the proposal. A couple of follow-ups from procurement/finance:

- BrightGrid policy requires the vendor form to capture primary contract terms (payment terms, indemnity caps, data residency fields). We'd prefer not to sign a separate MSA in practice — we'd rather the vendor form be the operative contract.
- Net-60 is required by our AP team unless vendor offers early-pay discounts. Net-45 will likely be a hard sell.
- We need Redwood's SOC2 Type II and W-9 before legal will accept anything. Please provide the SOC2 under NDA if needed.
- We also asked for a formal escalation/credits policy for outages that impact SLA.

If Redwood cannot make the vendor form the primary agreement, procurement will likely escalate and request legal review. Can Redwood confirm whether it will accept vendor form terms without reintroducing MSA language?

Thanks,
Karen
[attachment: BrightGrid_VendorForm_Filled.pdf]
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Karen Lin <karen.lin@brightgrid.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vendor form + pricing clarification for Hosted API commit — next steps

Karen — appreciate the transparency from procurement. To summarize Redwood's final position and proposed path to close: 

1) Vendor form: Redwood can accept BrightGrid's vendor form for PO creation and remit setup, but we cannot accept it as the sole governing contract without a brief legal review and a limited set of carve-ins. The primary reason is that our MSA contains operational SLA definitions, security obligations (data handling, KV caching rules, customer-controlled encryption), and indemnity language that we cannot remove wholesale. That said, we are open to a short addendum or a one-page SOW that references BrightGrid's vendor form for administrative fields and Redwood's MSA for service terms.

2) Payment terms: we can accept Net-60 for this enterprise deal contingent on finance credit approval; if BrightGrid can provide a PO and commit to a 12-month volume tier, Redwood will offer a 10% one-time first-year concession on the committed rate (in addition to the tier discount).

3) Compliance docs: we'll share SOC2 Type II and W-9 via a protected link/NDA by EOD tomorrow.

4) SLA & credits: our standard SLA and credit policy are included in the MSA/SOW; we will highlight the escalation path and provide a short appendix for BrightGrid if required.

Next steps I recommend:
- Vanessa/Redwood legal will send a one-page SOW referencing: commit tier, billing cadence, overage rule, SLA highlights.
- BrightGrid returns signed vendor form for PO + countersign SOW (or confirms acceptance of the SOW language) so we can route for revenue ops.
- Finance does credit approval for Net-60 (if approved, we apply the 10% concession as noted).

I'll have Priyom circulate the SOW draft this afternoon. Can you confirm who on your side we should send the SOC2 NDA and the DocuSign link to?

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_sow_draft_placeholder.pdf]
